newsitem.title: USA: Sequent stock jumps on news of order from Boeing.
newsitem.headline: Sequent stock jumps on news of order from Boeing.

text.p: Sequent Computer Systems Inc. stock jumped Monday after the company announced a record order and said it planned to raise about $125 million through a secondary stock offering.

Sequent, which makes powerful computers that compete with larger mainframe machines, said it had landed a contract with Boeing Co. worth $59 million, which could rise to $105 million over the next nine months if all options are exercised.
Last year Sequent's total revenue was about $595 million, although executives said the company, based in Beaverton, Ore., is on track for growth of more than 30 percent.

Sequent said the deal will allow it to report net income of $7.5 million to $8.5 million, or 20 cents to 23 cents a share, for the latest quarter on revenue of about $207 million, in line with analysts' estimates.
"I wouldn't see any reason for analysts to raise their estimates," Sequent Chairman Casey Powell said in an interview.
In last year's second quarter the company posted net income of $3.3 million or 10 cents a share on revenue of $143 million.
Sequent stock rose $1.25 to $25, its highest level in nearly two years, in heavy trading on Nasdaq.

Powell said the sale to Boeing represented the strongest vote of confidence in Sequent's NUMA-Q 2000 series of computers launched late last year. The computers can link dozens or even hundreds of Intel Corp. microprocessors to give the capability of a mainframe computer at a far lower price.

"I think it's a good indicator of what this product represents -- a real breakthrough in price performance," Powell said of the sale to Boeing, which will use the machines to overhaul its database systems.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Sequent said 5.25 million shares would be sold in the secondary offering, with 4.2 million shares being sold by the company and the rest by selling shareholders led by State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Co.
With an additional allotment of up to 787,500 shares for underwriters, the company could raise about $125 million at the stock's current price.
